source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:4 ('וישקהו — dotted with SIX dots, a dot on every letter: Bereshit Rabbah, Shir HaShirim Rabbah, the Zohar; Pirkei de-R. Eliezer: read not he-KISSED him but he-BIT him') + Kitzur ('dotted above — he meant to bite him')
claim_en: THE SIX-DOTTED KISS: וישקהו ('and he fell on his neck AND KISSED HIM, and they wept,' 33:4) — the fourth of the TEN DOTTED PLACES reached in canon order, and SNAPSHOT carries all SIX dots, one over each letter, exactly as Bereshit Rabbah counts them (DB-checked at the codepoint level): the tradition that reads the kiss as a bite riding letter by letter in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:4 ('צוארו — read צואריו per the Masorah; so Chizkuni; the Zohar carries a teaching on it')
claim_en: THE NECK WRITTEN ONE, READ MANY: צוארו ('he fell on his NECK,' 33:4) — the Masorah reads the plural ('his necks,' with yod); the letter writes the singular, no yod in the stream (DB-checked): a written/read split carried here as a single written-form token — unlike the two-token encoding at 8:17, the instrument varying by site as previously characterized.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 33:14 ('שעירה — three in the Masorah: to-my-lord-to-Seir, Esau-returned-to-Seir, the-bare-mountain-rising-to-Seir (Joshua); and the FINAL letters of until-I-come-to-my-lord-to-Seir spell אליה — he will come to him after the four exiles, before the great day, when the saviors ascend Mount Zion to judge Esau's mountain')
claim_en: ELIJAH IN THE FINALS OF THE SEIR PROMISE: אבא אל אדני שעירה ('until I COME to my lord, to Seir,' 33:14 — the visit Jacob never pays in his lifetime) — the four words' final letters spell אליה (Elijah, DB-checked in order): the Kitzur reads the deferred arrival as the end of days, when the saviors ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau (Obadiah, named). And the place-word itself stands exactly twice in the Torah, both in this meeting (33:14, 33:16, builder-checked), the Joshua member outside.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:1 ('וירא והנה — with GALGAL, not with maqqef; so Ben Asher's variant-lists') + 33:10 ('כי על כן — כי with GALGAL, not with maqqef')
claim_en: THE WHEEL-ACCENT'S TWO STATIONS: at the lifting of the eyes ('and he saw, AND BEHOLD, Esau coming,' 33:1) and at the gift-plea ('FOR therefore I have seen your face,' 33:10) Minchat Shai rules galgal (the wheel-accent), not maqqef — and SNAPSHOT carries NO maqqef at either station exactly as ruled (DB-checked), but stores the munach stroke where the wheel should turn: the galgal-vs-munach variance class grows to three stations (with 29:27), the layer's second and third source-anchored members.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:5 ('אלה לך — the lamed DAGESHED')
claim_en: WHO ARE THESE TO YOU — THE JOINED DAGESH: לך ('who are these TO YOU?', 33:5 — Esau over the children) — the lamed dageshed exactly as ruled, the joining dot after the open vowel binding the question to its object.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:8 ('פגשתי — the gimel in QAMATZ in the precise manuscripts and old prints; so Or Torah, against the printer's emendation')
claim_en: I-HAVE-MET IN QAMATZ: פגשתי ('all this camp that I MET,' 33:8) — the gimel in qamatz (the long a) with the precise manuscripts and Or Torah against the printer's emendation, at the pause of the etnachta.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 33:8 ('מי לך — three in the Masorah: who-is-to-you this whole camp; who-is-to-you here, that you hewed a tomb (Isa 22:16); who-else-is-to-you here — Lot at Sodom: the angel-companies striking Esau's men until they hewed graves') + MS 33:12 ('לנגדך — the gimel soft') + Kitzur 33:12 (the pair with Ps 90:8: 'why walk beside me and remember my sins BEFORE YOU')
claim_en: WHO-IS-TO-YOU, TWICE IN THE TORAH: the question-pair מי לך stands exactly twice — the angel at Sodom to Lot ('WHO else is TO YOU here?', 19:12) and Jacob's meeting ('WHO is all this camp TO YOU?', 33:8, builder-checked), the tomb-hewer of Isaiah named third; and Esau's offered escort is declined in a soft letter — לנגדך ('let me go BESIDE YOU,' 33:12) with the gimel soft as ruled, the word itself Torah-unique, its Masorah partner the psalm's 'our sins set BEFORE YOU' (Ps 90:8, named) — the Kitzur hearing Jacob's refusal inside it.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:13 ('הילדים — every the-children in Scripture: the he WITHOUT the stress-stroke; the Michlol')
claim_en: THE CHILDREN'S UNSTROKED HE: הילדים ('my lord knows that THE CHILDREN are tender,' 33:13) — the Michlol's rule that the-children never takes the stress-stroke on its he holds across all seven Torah tokens (builder-checked, five of them in this unit; the midwives' two at Exodus 1 carry only the verse-end stroke): the tender ones carried lightly in the pointing itself.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:10 ('כראת פני אלהים — PROFANE, tractate Soferim ch. 4') + Kitzur ('the count of the words equals your-prince: he hinted — I saw your angel and was saved')
claim_en: THE PROFANE SIGHT (classification layer, uninstrumented): 'for I have seen your face AS ONE SEES THE FACE OF אלהים' (33:10) — tractate Soferim rules this Name PROFANE (a great one's face, Esau's own angel per the Kitzur's count); the stream carries no holy/profane layer — station eleven filed. The seeing-word itself כראת is written lean, no vav (DB-checked), against the full form the Kitzur's citation carries.
